ata.title: Forward Fuselage Wiring — Avionics Bay Harnesses

abstract: Wiring sheet for the avionics bay harnesses serving the recorder, navigation and data loading racks, with the separation rule between the switched bundle and the antenna feeds.

sections.purpose: This sheet shows the avionics bay harnesses serving the recorder rack, the navigation rack and the data loading interface, with the connector list and the separation rules that apply inside the bay.
sections.sheet_note: The sheet is drawn looking forward with the racks in their delivered positions. The switched bundle is shown in heavy line; every antenna feed must keep 200 millimetres from it over its whole run, which is the constraint that drove the navigation feed reroute. Rack positions carrying isolated trays are marked, because the harness at those positions needs a free travel allowance that the sheet states at the clamp.
sections.routing_note: Harnesses run along the bay wall from the forward penetration to each rack, supported at 250 millimetre intervals and clamped at every rack entry. At isolated tray positions the clamp must leave 15 millimetres of free travel; a harness pulled tight across an isolator defeats the isolation and is the most common installation error in this bay.
